trust_decision.summary: An outbound request is trusted only because its URL string passes one synchronous check: http/https protocol, hostname not in the BLOCKED_HOSTNAMES set, hostname not a blocked IPv4/IPv6 *literal*, and (optionally) hostname in CKAN_ALLOWED_DOMAINS — decided in validateServerUrl at src/utils/http.ts:245. What the hostname actually resolves to is never checked, so any DNS name pointing at an internal address is trusted.

landing_point.why: The report is 'SSRF via DNS-name to internal IP'; validateServerUrl is the only SSRF filter in the tree and the function every CKAN tool reaches through makeCkanRequest, so an engineer searches for it and edits the hostname/private-IP test there.

fix_sites.entry_point: every tool that takes a caller-supplied URL (19 ckan_* tools) plus the 4 CKAN MCP resources, all via makeCkanRequest
makeCkanRequest — the single axios call used by all CKAN tools and resources

fix_sites.module_kind: MCP tool with its own fetch implementation

O3_reason_to_dismiss: sparql_query is not a CKAN server_url: it is a separate HTTPS-only, read-only tool with its own protocol check, so the CKAN API guard is argued not to apply to it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Documented portal aliases and their http-to-https upgrade must keep working: http://dati.gov.it/opendata and https://dati.gov.it are accepted and then rewritten to https://www.dati.gov.it/opendata, a different hostname, so an over-broad fix that requires https, or demands the resolved/requested host equal the supplied host, breaks aliased portals.

O6_input_shapes: bracketed IPv6 literal, including loopback ::1, unique-local fc00::/7, link-local fe80::/10 and ::ffff:-mapped forms
DNS hostname that resolves to an internal IPv4 or IPv6 address (wildcard DNS such as lvh.me, *.nip.io)
hostname with several A/AAAA records where only one resolves internally
the address a redirect reconnects to, rather than the initially validated URL
the same hostname arriving over the fetch transport (sparql) rather than axios (CKAN API)
http vs https and alias / trailing-slash URL forms that are rewritten by portals.json

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The non-Node fetch branch of makeCkanRequest sends the request with no IP or DNS guard; the published fix installs its SSRF-safe lookup agents only inside the isNode branch, leaving this branch unchanged.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It only runs off Node (Cloudflare Workers), where the CF sandbox already blocks internal addresses and node:dns is unavailable — the fix's own changelog states the Worker is unaffected.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function, other runtime branch; used from src/worker.ts:20

O8_uncovered_routes.route: querySparqlEndpoint validates only the initial endpoint hostname; the fetch calls still follow redirects (default fetch behaviour), so a public HTTPS SPARQL endpoint that answers 302 to an internal address is followed without re-checking the new host.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Redirects from a public SPARQL endpoint are ordinary and the endpoint URL itself was validated; only the first hop is in scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, second hop after the guard

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A resource-download / preview tool that fetches a resource's download_url (resolveDownloadUrl, src/tools/package.ts:251-257) directly instead of going through makeCkanRequest.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The repo already probes other portals from resource URLs (checkSourceDatastore, ckan_list_resources), so a maintainer adding 'download this CSV' would naturally request the resource URL itself.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second metadata-enrichment client (MQA / data.europa.eu) that calls axios and fetch directly, outside makeCkanRequest, built partly from dataset metadata.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This file already bypasses the shared request function and builds its URLs from a dataset identifier returned by the portal.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A registry/discovery client with its own axios call and no validateServerUrl call at all.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the only tool with a hard-coded third-party host, the obvious template for a second discovery source.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A runtime-specific HTTP branch (Workers/edge) beside the Node one, needing its own duplicate of the guard.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The codebase already maintains duplicate request logic for Node and non-Node runtimes.

O9_family: SSRF (CWE-918): server-side request forgery where a hostname is allowed because only its string form is checked, not the address it resolves to

O10_build.language: TypeScript (ESM, Node >=18; also bundled for Cloudflare Workers)
O10_build.toolchain: npm; esbuild bundle (npm run build), tsc (npm run build:tsc), vitest (npm test)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/unit/http.test.ts:10 (validateServerUrl) and :80 (makeCkanRequest, axios mocked via vi.mock('axios') at :8); tests/integration/sparql.test.ts stubs global fetch. Both suites run offline. No DNS-resolution test exists at the pinned commit.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Extend the synchronous hostname test in validateServerUrl (or add one dns.lookup before the axios call) so the CKAN API path rejects names resolving to private IPs — a single pre-resolution check with no connection pinning, no redirect hop and no coverage of the fetch-based sparql path.

out_of_scope_notes: Earlier sibling SSRF advisories in the same package (GHSA-3xm7-qw7j-qc8v, GHSA-g84h-j7jj-x32p) are recorded in LOG.md:13 and LOG.md:159-163; not pursued beyond noting the pattern.

src/tools/quality.ts and src/tools/portal-discovery.ts make direct axios/fetch calls to hard-coded third-party hosts (src/tools/quality.ts:12-13, src/tools/portal-discovery.ts:11); their target hosts are not caller-controlled.
unverified: Repository size in MB was not measured (no shell available); O4.repo_mb is null.
src/server.ts:22 and src/worker.ts:223 are version-string-only changes in the fix and were not counted as security sites.

Whether the fixed isBlockedIp rejects every textual IP form the OS resolver accepts (e.g. 2130706433, fully expanded ::ffff:7f00:1) was not verified; on the axios path the connection-time lookup would still see the resolved internal address, so it was not recorded as an uncovered route.
Whether the hidden behavioural tests can drive the non-Node fetch branch at all was not checked; O8 entry 1 may not be reachable from a Node test harness.
